Enforce heartbeat and start-to-close timeouts in test environment (#2144)

* Enforce heartbeat and start-to-close timeouts in test environment

This extends the existing heartbeat timeout enforcement to also enforce
StartToCloseTimeout in the test environment. The implementation uses a
unified timeout monitoring goroutine that checks both timeout types.

Changes:
- Renamed heartbeatTimeoutResult to activityTimeoutResult with timeoutType field
- Extended testActivityHandle to track both timeout types and activity start time
- Unified monitoring goroutine checks both heartbeat and start-to-close timeouts
- The timeout that fires first wins (heartbeat if shorter, start-to-close otherwise)

This addresses https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-go/issues/1282

* Fix StartToCloseTimeout cause to be context.DeadlineExceeded

When the monitoring goroutine detects a StartToCloseTimeout, the
cause should be context.DeadlineExceeded since we set up the context
deadline to match the timeout. This maintains backward compatibility
with the existing Test_ActivityDeadlineExceeded test which expects
the timeout error's cause to be "context deadline exceeded".

* Add configurable grace period for activity timeout enforcement

Add SetActivityTimeoutGracePeriod() method to TestWorkflowEnvironment
that allows configuring how long the test framework waits after the
StartToCloseTimeout expires before forcibly timing out activities.

This gives well-behaved activities that respect ctx.Done() a chance to
return gracefully before being timed out externally. Default is 0 (no
grace period) to maintain backward compatibility.

* Add tests for SetActivityTimeoutGracePeriod option

Add two tests to verify the grace period behavior:
- Test_ActivityStartToCloseTimeout_GracePeriod: Verifies that an activity
  completing within timeout + grace period times out via the normal
  context.DeadlineExceeded path (not the monitoring goroutine)
- Test_ActivityStartToCloseTimeout_GracePeriodExceeded: Verifies that an
  activity exceeding timeout + grace period is forcibly timed out by the
  monitoring goroutine

Nexus caller timeouts (#2146)

## Overview

Implements two new granular timeout types for Nexus operations, allowing callers to have fine-grained control over different phases of operation execution:

- **Schedule-to-Start Timeout**: Maximum time to wait for an operation to be started (or completed if synchronous) by the handler
- **Start-to-Close Timeout**: Maximum time to wait for an asynchronous operation to complete after it has been started

These timeouts complement the existing **Schedule-to-Close Timeout** to provide better control and diagnostics for Nexus operation execution.

See also https://github.com/temporalio/api/pull/695 and the corresponding server PR: https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/pull/9010.

Fix standalone activity result long-poll bug (#2198)

* Failing test for standalone activity poll context bug

Add unit test that verifies PollActivityResult creates a fresh gRPC
context per poll iteration with pollActivityTimeout (60s), rather than
sharing a single context with defaultRPCTimeout (10s).

* Fix standalone activity result long-poll bug

Create a fresh gRPC context per poll iteration instead of sharing one
across the loop. The shared context's deadline would expire after the
first iteration, causing subsequent polls to fail immediately.

Also use an explicit pollActivityTimeout (60s) rather than inheriting
defaultRPCTimeout (10s) which is too short for long-poll operations.

* Fix Windows CI: compare context identity not deadlines

The deadline-based assertion failed on Windows where coarse timer
resolution means consecutive time.Now() calls return the same value.
Compare context pointers instead, which directly tests the invariant
(each poll iteration creates a fresh context).

Add Serialization context for codecs and converters (#2225)

* Add SerializationContext for DataConverter, PayloadCodec, and FailureConverter

Introduces an opt-in mechanism that provides metadata (namespace, workflow ID,
activity type, etc.) to converter implementations during serialization. This
enables use cases like per-workflow encryption using workflow ID as associated
data for a key.

Adds WorkflowSerializationContext (for workflow-level payloads) and
ActivitySerializationContext (for activity-level payloads), with opt-in
interfaces for DataConverter, PayloadCodec, and FailureConverter.

Context is provided at every serialization site: workflow execution, activity,
local activity, child workflow, signal, query, update, continue-as-new, side
effect, client operations, schedule client, and async activity completion.

Matches the feature already implemented in Python, .NET, and Java SDKs.

Closes #1352

* Fix continue-as-new detection in workflowstreams Subscribe

followContinueAsNew described the workflow with an empty run id, which returns
the current run. After a continue-as-new that is the new RUNNING run, never
CONTINUED_AS_NEW (which only sits on the old, closed run), so the check never
fired and Subscribe stopped or surfaced an error during a routine rollover
instead of following the stream into the successor run.

Capture the run id each poll's update is admitted to (wait only for ACCEPTED so
the handle — and its RunID — is returned even when the run continues-as-new
before the outcome), and describe that specific run on failure. A rolled-over
run reports CONTINUED_AS_NEW, a terminal run reports a terminal status, and a
still-RUNNING run means a transient error that should surface. This also avoids
mistaking an unrelated new execution that reused the workflow id for a successor.

Honor context cancellation in ResourceBasedSlotSupplier.ReserveSlot (#2458)

ReserveSlot only observed its context while the ramp throttle was actively
making the caller wait. With RampThrottle == 0 (the workflow default), or once
the last issuance was long enough ago that no wait was required, the retry loop
had no cancellation point: it ended in a bare time.Sleep and only exited by
obtaining a permit. TryReserveSlot returns nil for as long as the controller
declines, which is the sustained resource pressure the tuner exists to handle.

reserveSlotAsync runs ReserveSlot on the worker's stop WaitGroup, so the
goroutine outlived the worker, reporting a graceful stop timeout and continuing
to sample system resources for the life of the process.

Check the context at the top of the loop, and make the retry wait cancellable.
FixedSizeSlotSupplier already behaves this way: semaphore.Acquire fails a
cancelled context even when it could acquire without blocking.

[AI-383] contrib/googleadk: add replay-safe OpenTelemetry provider wrappers (#2514)

* Add replay-safe OTel provider wrappers to googleadk contrib

ADK records spans, gen_ai.* log events, and (future) metrics through the
OpenTelemetry process globals from code that runs inside the workflow, so
every history replay re-emitted one full copy of all of it. Wrap the global
tracer/logger/meter providers so emissions from replaying workflow code are
dropped while first-execution and non-workflow telemetry pass through
unchanged.

* Return usable instrument from meter wrapper on constructor error

The OTel SDK meter returns a functional instrument alongside a non-nil
error (e.g. invalid instrument name); the replay-safe meter discarded it
and returned nil, nil-panicking callers that follow the OTel contract.
Wrap whatever non-nil instrument the inner meter returns and propagate
the error. Also assert the ungated replay-inflation control test on the
replay-added delta so a sticky-cache miss during the live run cannot
flake it, and document the sticky-cache-eviction span caveat in the
README.

* Pass span start options through suppressed tracer

The noop tracer ignores options, so behavior is unchanged, but the
passthrough keeps the wrapper aligned with the trace.Tracer contract.

* Warn at worker start when global OTel providers are not replay-safe

* Document span loss and at-least-once caveats for replay-safe telemetry

* Classify deprecated and pointer-wrapped noop providers as replay-safe

* Detect non-replay-safe providers by public OTel SDK types

Replace the reflect PkgPath heuristic (matching OTel's internal/global
package path) with type assertions against the public SDK provider
types. The worker-start warning now fires only on a positively
recognized raw SDK provider; wrappers, noops, never-set proxies, and
custom providers stay silent. The SDK modules were already direct
requirements of this module.

* Correct meter provider install-order godoc

* Mention replay-safe telemetry wrappers in package doc

* Cover every sync instrument gate and Enabled under replay

* Warn on raw global OTel providers at replayer creation too

The warning previously fired only at worker start; a workflow replayer
re-emits ADK telemetry through raw global providers on every replayed
history, so it needs the same warning. ConfigureWorkflowReplayer fires
once per replayer construction, matching the Python plugin's
worker/replayer symmetry. The hook wiring test lives in its own
test-only package because it must bind the one-shot OTel global proxy.

contrib/googleadk: harden replay-safe telemetry wrappers (#2573)

* Gate sync instrument Enabled during replay

OTel metric v1.43.0 gives synchronous instruments an Enabled(ctx) hint;
the wrappers previously let it pass through ungated via embedding. Report
false while the matching Add/Record would be dropped, mirroring
replaySafeLogger.Enabled, and count Enabled like the recording methods in
the gate-coverage test.

* Add surface-drift guard for replay-safe wrappers

OTel Go grows its telemetry interfaces between minor releases via the
embedded.* types, and any method a wrapper does not declare is promoted
from the embedded inner value and delegates ungated. Fail on promoted
methods that are neither declared nor allowlisted with a rationale, and
self-test the classifier on a simulated interface growth.

* Pin query and update validator replay-gate behavior

Update validators never run during replay (accepted updates skip
validation and new updates land in the live batch), so validator-time
telemetry always records. Query handlers inherit the last processed
event's replay flag: served right after a catch-up replay whose trailing
event is a command or completion event they observe IsReplaying true and
the gate drops the live recording — the same semantics as
workflow.GetMetricsHandler. Pin both with dev-server probes and document
the non-bridged-context workaround for query-time telemetry.

* Note pre-1.0 OTel Logs API status in README

go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log is v0.x: the Logs Bridge API may change
between minor releases, and the surface-drift test audits any growth
against the replay gate.

* Assert gated Enabled polarity in replay probe

The gate probe discarded Enabled's return value, so a wrapper returning
true while replaying would still pass; the workflow now requires
Enabled == !IsReplaying at every probe, live and replayed.

* Make liveops query poll non-fatal and trim comments

require inside Eventually's polling goroutine is unsafe; poll through a
require-free tryQuery. Also corrects the header: a new finer core
predicate would not fail these pins — only a change in what queries
observe would.

Deduplicate the meter Enabled contract into one doc comment, halve the
README additions, tighten the changelog bullet, and note that thunk
detection is a gc toolchain detail whose breakage fails the guard
loudly.

* Retry transient query RPC errors in liveops probes

* Compose replay gate with workflow.IsReadOnly

main-branch pseudo-version of go.temporal.io/sdk until a tagged
release ships workflow.IsReadOnly.

* Tolerate query re-dispatch in liveops probe counts

The server may re-dispatch a query task whose response was lost or
timed out, legitimately re-running the handler, so exact counter

contrib/googleadk: adopt adk/v2 v2.2.0 and multi-decision confirmation resumes (#2538)

Bump google.golang.org/adk/v2 from the July-7 main pseudo-version to the
tagged v2.2.0 release. The platform provider seams this plugin consumes
(the TaskRunner/time/UUID providers, tool/toolutils.PackTool, and the
model.Register/NewLLM registry) have been in tagged releases since
v2.1.0; v2.2.0 is the first tag with the request-order confirmation
resume (google/adk-go#1169), which multi-decision confirmation resumes
need to schedule their Activities replay-stably — hence the v2.2.0
minimum.

With that fix, a resume message carrying two or more tool confirmations
re-queues the approved calls of each confirmation request in the order
the paused calls appeared in (a batch spanning multiple pause events
resumes the newest event first), never in the order of the decisions in
the resume message, so batched resumes that dispatch Temporal Activities
are replay-stable. Rewrite the ConfirmationResponse doc to that
contract, replace the stale go.mod pin rationale with the v2.2.0 minimum
rationale, record the inherited Go 1.26.5+ floor (as a breaking change)
and the adk-raised genai v1.66.0 floor in the CHANGELOG, drop the
one-decision-per-pass guidance, and refresh the README install note
that described the pseudo-version pin.

Add TestHITLMultiDecisionBatchedResume, which drives the previously
hazardous shape end to end: one scripted model turn calls three guarded
ActivityAsTool tools (wrapped with ADK's standard tool.WithConfirmation
guard) in request order alpha, beta, gamma; all three pause;
PendingConfirmations surfaces all three; and a single batched
ConfirmationResponse — decisions deliberately rotated to (gamma, alpha,
beta), matching neither the request order nor its reverse — executes
each underlying Activity exactly once. Strict order assertions pin that
the resumed tool responses follow the confirmations' request order
regardless of decision position, a deterministic catch for any
wrong-order regression that keys on decision order. They do not
probabilistically re-prove upstream's map-iteration fix (Go's small-map
iteration is insertion-biased, so a map-order regression can pass an
individual run; upstream pins that with its own
TestRequestConfirmationResumeOrderIsStable). Extend
TestReplaySingleAndMultiAgent with the same workflow and assertions so
its recorded history replays through worker.WorkflowReplayer, guarding
the Temporal-side determinism contract.

* contrib/googleadk: export the active workflow.Context accessor

Fixes #2683

An in-workflow ADK tool that wants to issue a workflow command of its own --
starting and awaiting a child workflow, a timer, a signal -- needs the
workflow.Context of the coroutine it is currently running on. The adapter
already stashes exactly that per coroutine, but under an unexported key
(wfCtxKey) read only by an unexported accessor (workflowContext), and a context
key of an unexported type is unforgeable from outside the package.

WorkflowContext exposes the existing lookup unchanged. No behavior, signature,
or existing exported symbol changes.

A tool cannot work around this by closing over the enclosing workflow
function's Context: during concurrent fan-out the tool runs on its own
coroutine while the coroutine owning the root Context is blocked on the fan-out
join, so a Future awaited there never resolves and the workflow task trips
deadlock detection. TestWorkflowContextRootContextFailsOnFanout pins that
failure mode, so the justification for the export is itself tested rather than
just asserted in a comment.

Tests (childworkflow_test.go, black-box, reusing the existing harness):
- concurrent fan-out: two tools each start and await their own child
- sequential fan-out: same, where tasks run on the calling coroutine
- children are recorded as real executions with the ids the tools chose
- a failing child surfaces to the tool instead of resolving silently
- the root-Context anti-pattern fails, and fails with a deadlock
- absent/nil contract: reports false rather than panicking
- outside fan-out the accessor returns the calling workflow's own Context

Validation: go test ./... green for the module; gofmt and go vet clean. The new
tests do not compile without the export (undefined: googleadk.WorkflowContext),
which is what makes this unachievable outside the package.
